dedupe_keys.name: highwayenv gymnasium environments for autonomous driving and tactical decision making farama foundation

description: HighwayEnv is a collection of lightweight driving simulation environments for training and testing reinforcement learning and planning agents on tactical decisions such as lane changes, merging and crossing intersections. It was created by Edouard Leurent and is now maintained by the Farama Foundation alongside Gymnasium. Coverage: generic synthetic road layouts, not real places. The environments include highway, merge, roundabout, parking, intersection, racetrack, lane keeping, two-way road, exit and U-turn scenes; each offers configurable observations (kinematics, grayscale images, occupancy grids, time to collision), discrete or continuous actions, simple vehicle dynamics with behaviour models for surrounding traffic (IDM car-following and MOBIL lane changes), road regulation rules, rewards and a multi-agent mode, and users can build their own environments. Format and access: Python package on PyPI and GitHub with documentation; free. Licence: MIT. Caveats: vehicle physics and traffic behaviour are simplified for fast learning, road networks are abstract, and results do not transfer directly to real traffic. Simulation uses: agent-based experiments on driver and automated vehicle behaviour at merges and intersections, and optimisation of control policies that affect road capacity. Related records: SUMO-RL (platform-sumo-rl) offers reinforcement learning on the SUMO traffic simulator, and CARLA (platform-carla) is a high-fidelity driving simulator.
